assets.subject: a human man of average build in plain clothes (a body reference)
assets.name: Human body reference (man)
assets.prompt:
Create a new single asset in the Turnip Works house style (heroic hand-painted): a painted tabletop miniature FIGURE of a human man of average build in plain clothes (a body reference).

The supplied image is ANOTHER FIGURE OF THE SAME SET, already made. The new figure must belong to the same set: the SAME painting style, the same chunkiness and level of detail, the same lighting, the same camera angle and the same flat blue background. It is a DIFFERENT character, described below: do not copy the reference's armour, colours, face or pose, and do NOT copy how far its sword and shield are held out to the sides.

Geometry: heroic-scale tabletop miniature proportions: stout and chunky, slightly oversized head, hands, feet and held things; thick limbs; broad simple shapes; deep readable folds and plates rather than fine detail. Hands are simple chunky fists or mitten shapes. Every part thick enough to reconstruct as 3D geometry and to survive as a printed tabletop piece.
Held things: BROAD and chunky, never thin: wide blades, big heads on hammers, maces, staffs and spears, thick shafts. They are PALE or BRIGHT (bone-white wood, bright steel, cream, brass) against the clothes and skin, never plain dark wood-brown, so they show when the figure is seen small from above.
Finish: FULLY PAINTED in full colour, diffuse-first hand-painted game art with broad soft gradients, subtle brush texture, sparing painted edge highlights, low-frequency surface detail, mostly matte. A simple readable painted face.
Palette: rich but softened burgundy, moss green, ochre, cream, warm honey leather and wood, warm grey steel, used where they suit the figure. NO blue, teal or cyan anywhere on the figure (the background is a blue mask).
Avoid: grey unpainted primer, bare plastic or pewter, a bronze or stone statue look; photorealism, plastic toy gloss, strong reflections, black outlines, hard cel-shading bands, comic inking, flat vector art, anime or chibi proportions; thin fragile parts, loose straps, flying cloaks, long capes, banners, chains, feathers or hair strands sticking out; glow, magic effects, sparks, smoke; text, logos, emblems; multiple views, variants, a turnaround sheet or a grid in one image.

Pose: ONE single full figure, the WHOLE body in frame from the top of the head to the soles of the feet, standing still and upright in a clear, stable, compact classic miniature pose (not a T-pose, not an action leap, not a crouch, not a wide stance). Feet shoulder-width apart with a clear gap between the legs, planted FLAT on the same level. COMPACT: the whole figure, with everything it holds, fits inside an upright cylinder 4 ft across; NOTHING is held out to the side at arm's length. Whatever it holds is held UPRIGHT and close, a hand's width in front of or beside the body, with clear background visible in the gap, so nothing fuses together. Elbows near the ribs.
NO BASE: no base, no ground disc, no plinth, no pedestal, no rock, no grass tuft, no patch of floor under the feet. The figure floats on the plain background, standing on nothing. No cast shadow and no dark blob under the feet.

Presentation for image-to-3D: exactly one complete figure, centered, three-quarter FRONT view (turned about 30 degrees, face and chest clearly visible) from very slightly above eye level, generous clear space around every edge, perfectly uniform solid chroma-blue background, no horizon, no floor plane, no cast shadow, neutral even lighting with no colored light casts and no dark shadowed side, no environment, no scenery, no additional objects or other figures. The blue background is a removable mask and must not reflect blue light onto the figure.

Specific design: A human man of average build; 6.0 ft tall. Plain, close-fitting clothes that show the body's build: a sleeveless cream tunic to the hip with a rope belt, ochre trousers to the ankle, simple shoes. Standing straight and relaxed, arms hanging a hand's width from the body, hands empty, looking forward. Nothing held, no hat, no cloak, no armour.

gate.desc: one human man in a plain tunic and trousers, standing, empty-handed
must: the whole figure head to toe, both feet visible
a visible gap between the two legs
empty hands (nothing held)
fully painted in colour

a cast shadow or dark blob under the feet

more than one figure, or several views of the figure

Geometry: heroic-scale tabletop miniature proportions: stout and chunky, slightly oversized head, hands, feet and held things; thick limbs; broad simple shapes; deep readable folds and plates rather than fine detail. Hands are simple chunky fists or mitten shapes. Every part thick enough to reconstruct as 3D geometry and to survive as a printed tabletop piece.
Held things: BROAD and chunky, never thin: wide blades, big heads on hammers, maces, staffs and spears, thick shafts. Palette: rich but softened burgundy, moss green, ochre, cream, warm honey leather and wood, warm grey steel, used where they suit the figure. NO blue, teal or cyan anywhere on the figure (the background is a blue mask).
Avoid: grey unpainted primer, bare plastic or pewter, a bronze or stone statue look; photorealism, plastic toy gloss, strong reflections, black outlines, hard cel-shading bands, comic inking, flat vector art, anime or chibi proportions; thin fragile parts, loose straps, flying cloaks, long capes, banners, chains, feathers or hair strands sticking out; glow, magic effects, sparks, smoke; text, logos, emblems; multiple views, variants, a turnaround sheet or a grid in one image.

The blue background is a removable mask and must not reflect blue light onto the figure.

SORCERER kit: NO gear at all (no staff, no book, no hat, no weapon) and flowing, un-wizardly clothes: a long open sleeveless ochre-gold coat with a wide burgundy sash over a cream shirt, loose burgundy trousers gathered at the ankle, bare forearms with broad brass bangles, hair (or crest) swept up as if by wind, drawn as one solid chunky shape. The supplied image is ANOTHER MEMBER OF THE SAME WARBAND, already made. The new figure is the same kind of creature: the SAME body proportions, size, skin or bone colour and features, the same rough style of clothing and gear, the same painting style, lighting, camera angle and flat blue background, so the two stand side by side as one people. It is a DIFFERENT individual with DIFFERENT gear and a different stance, described below: its silhouette must be clearly different from the reference's.

Geometry: heroic-scale tabletop miniature proportions: stout and chunky, slightly oversized head, hands, feet and held things; thick limbs; broad simple shapes; deep readable folds and plates rather than fine detail. Hands are simple chunky fists or mitten shapes. Every part thick enough to reconstruct as 3D geometry and to survive as a printed tabletop piece.
Held things: BROAD and chunky, never thin: wide blades, big heads on hammers, maces, staffs and spears, thick shafts. They are PALE or BRIGHT (bone-white wood, bright steel, cream, brass) against the clothes and skin, never plain dark wood-brown, so they show when the figure is seen small from above.
Finish: FULLY PAINTED in full colour, diffuse-first hand-painted game art with broad soft gradients, subtle brush texture, sparing painted edge highlights, low-frequency surface detail, mostly matte. A simple readable painted face.
Palette: rich but softened burgundy, moss green, ochre, cream, warm honey leather and wood, warm grey steel, used where they suit the figure. NO blue, teal or cyan anywhere on the figure (the background is a blue mask).
Avoid: grey unpainted primer, bare plastic or pewter, a bronze or stone statue look; photorealism, plastic toy gloss, strong reflections, black outlines, hard cel-shading bands, comic inking, flat vector art, anime or chibi proportions; thin fragile parts, loose straps, flying cloaks, long capes, banners, chains, feathers or hair strands sticking out; glow, magic effects, sparks, smoke; text, logos, emblems; multiple views, variants, a turnaround sheet or a grid in one image.

Pose: ONE single full figure, the WHOLE body in frame from the top of the head to the soles of the feet, standing still and upright in a clear, stable, compact classic miniature pose (not a T-pose, not an action leap, not a crouch, not a wide stance). Feet shoulder-width apart with a clear gap between the legs, planted FLAT on the same level. COMPACT: the whole figure, with everything it holds, fits inside an upright cylinder 4 ft across; NOTHING is held out to the side at arm's length. Whatever it holds is held UPRIGHT and close, a hand's width in front of or beside the body, with clear background visible in the gap, so nothing fuses together. Elbows near the ribs.
NO BASE: no base, no ground disc, no plinth, no pedestal, no rock, no grass tuft, no patch of floor under the feet. The figure floats on the plain background, standing on nothing. No cast shadow and no dark blob under the feet.

The blue background is a removable mask and must not reflect blue light onto the figure.

A cream shirt, an ochre leather vest, moss-green trousers, tall boots, a broad belt with a big brass buckle. The bandit CAPTAIN: a broad-brimmed ochre hat, a long dark burgundy coat with brass buttons over a mail shirt, a broad cream sash, tall boots. Create a new single asset in the Turnip Works house style (heroic hand-painted): a painted tabletop miniature FIGURE of a giant centipede.

The supplied image is ANOTHER FIGURE OF THE SAME SET, already made. The new figure must belong to the same set: the SAME painting style, the same chunkiness and level of detail, the same lighting, the same camera angle and the same flat blue background. It is a DIFFERENT character, described below: do not copy the reference's armour, colours, face or pose, and do NOT copy how far its sword and shield are held out to the sides.

Geometry: heroic-scale tabletop miniature proportions: stout and chunky, slightly oversized head, hands, feet and held things; thick limbs; broad simple shapes; deep readable folds and plates rather than fine detail. Hands are simple chunky fists or mitten shapes. Every part thick enough to reconstruct as 3D geometry and to survive as a printed tabletop piece.
Held things: BROAD and chunky, never thin: wide blades, big heads on hammers, maces, staffs and spears, thick shafts. They are PALE or BRIGHT (bone-white wood, bright steel, cream, brass) against the clothes and skin, never plain dark wood-brown, so they show when the figure is seen small from above.
Finish: FULLY PAINTED in full colour, diffuse-first hand-painted game art with broad soft gradients, subtle brush texture, sparing painted edge highlights, low-frequency surface detail, mostly matte. A simple readable painted face.
Palette: rich but softened burgundy, moss green, ochre, cream, warm honey leather and wood, warm grey steel, used where they suit the figure. NO blue, teal or cyan anywhere on the figure (the background is a blue mask).
Avoid: grey unpainted primer, bare plastic or pewter, a bronze or stone statue look; photorealism, plastic toy gloss, strong reflections, black outlines, hard cel-shading bands, comic inking, flat vector art, anime or chibi proportions; thin fragile parts, loose straps, flying cloaks, long capes, banners, chains, feathers or hair strands sticking out; glow, magic effects, sparks, smoke; text, logos, emblems; multiple views, variants, a turnaround sheet or a grid in one image.

Pose: ONE single whole creature in frame, top to bottom, at rest in a clear, stable, compact pose, its underside flat on one level as if on an invisible floor. COMPACT: all of it fits inside an upright cylinder 4 ft across; nothing stretched far out to the side.
NO BASE: no base, no ground disc, no plinth, no pedestal, no rock, no grass tuft, no patch of floor under the feet. The figure floats on the plain background, standing on nothing. No cast shadow and no dark blob under the feet.

Presentation for image-to-3D: exactly one complete figure, centered, three-quarter FRONT view (turned about 30 degrees, face and chest clearly visible) from very slightly above eye level, generous clear space around every edge, perfectly uniform solid chroma-blue background, no horizon, no floor plane, no cast shadow, neutral even lighting with no colored light casts and no dark shadowed side, no environment, no scenery, no additional objects or other figures. The blue background is a removable mask and must not reflect blue light onto the figure.

Specific design: A giant centipede 1.5 ft tall, curled in a tight S so it fits in a 4-ft circle: about ten thick glossy burgundy-brown armour segments, each with a pair of very thick, short ochre legs flat on the ground, a broad head with two thick curved fangs and two short thick feelers.

gate.desc: one giant centipede with many thick short legs, curled
must: the whole creature, nothing cut off
a long segmented body with many legs
fully painted in colour
must_not: any base, ground disc, plinth, pedestal, rock or patch of ground under the feet
a cast shadow or dark blob under the feet
the figure cropped by the frame anywhere (head, hat, weapon tip, feet, tail)
limbs fused together or fused to the body with no gap where the spec asks for a gap

more than one figure, or several views of the figure

The supplied image is ANOTHER FIGURE OF THE SAME SET, already made. The new figure must belong to the same set: the SAME painting style, the same chunkiness and level of detail, the same lighting, the same camera angle and the same flat blue background. It is a DIFFERENT character, described below: do not copy the reference's armour, colours, face or pose, and do NOT copy how far its sword and shield are held out to the sides.

Geometry: heroic-scale tabletop miniature proportions: stout and chunky, slightly oversized head, hands, feet and held things; thick limbs; broad simple shapes; deep readable folds and plates rather than fine detail. Hands are simple chunky fists or mitten shapes. Every part thick enough to reconstruct as 3D geometry and to survive as a printed tabletop piece.
Held things: BROAD and chunky, never thin: wide blades, big heads on hammers, maces, staffs and spears, thick shafts. They are PALE or BRIGHT (bone-white wood, bright steel, cream, brass) against the clothes and skin, never plain dark wood-brown, so they show when the figure is seen small from above.
Finish: FULLY PAINTED in full colour, diffuse-first hand-painted game art with broad soft gradients, subtle brush texture, sparing painted edge highlights, low-frequency surface detail, mostly matte. A simple readable painted face.
Palette: rich but softened burgundy, moss green, ochre, cream, warm honey leather and wood, warm grey steel, used where they suit the figure. NO blue, teal or cyan anywhere on the figure (the background is a blue mask).
Avoid: grey unpainted primer, bare plastic or pewter, a bronze or stone statue look; photorealism, plastic toy gloss, strong reflections, black outlines, hard cel-shading bands, comic inking, flat vector art, anime or chibi proportions; thin fragile parts, loose straps, flying cloaks, long capes, banners, chains, feathers or hair strands sticking out; glow, magic effects, sparks, smoke; text, logos, emblems; multiple views, variants, a turnaround sheet or a grid in one image.

Pose: ONE single full figure, the WHOLE body in frame from the top of the head to the soles of the feet, standing still and upright in a clear, stable, compact classic miniature pose (not a T-pose, not an action leap, not a crouch, not a wide stance). Feet shoulder-width apart with a clear gap between the legs, planted FLAT on the same level. COMPACT: the whole figure, with everything it holds, fits inside an upright cylinder 8.5 ft across; NOTHING is held out to the side at arm's length. Whatever it holds is held UPRIGHT and close, a hand's width in front of or beside the body, with clear background visible in the gap, so nothing fuses together. Elbows near the ribs.
NO BASE: no base, no ground disc, no plinth, no pedestal, no rock, no grass tuft, no patch of floor under the feet. The figure floats on the plain background, standing on nothing. No cast shadow and no dark blob under the feet.

Presentation for image-to-3D: exactly one complete figure, centered, three-quarter FRONT view (turned about 30 degrees, face and chest clearly visible) from very slightly above eye level, generous clear space around every edge, perfectly uniform solid chroma-blue background, no horizon, no floor plane, no cast shadow, neutral even lighting with no colored light casts and no dark shadowed side, no environment, no scenery, no additional objects or other figures. The blue background is a removable mask and must not reflect blue light onto the figure.

Specific design: An iron golem, 10 ft tall: a towering armoured giant built of dark riveted iron plates with brass bands, a helmet-shaped head with a grille and no face, massive shoulders, thick piston-like limbs. Its RIGHT fist holds a huge broad iron SWORD standing point-down at ground level close beside its leg; its left fist hangs at its side.

assets.prompt:
Create a new single asset in the Turnip Works house style (heroic hand-painted): a painted tabletop miniature FIGURE of a frost giant.

The supplied image is ANOTHER FIGURE OF THE SAME SET, already made. The new figure must belong to the same set: the SAME painting style, the same chunkiness and level of detail, the same lighting, the same camera angle and the same flat blue background. It is a DIFFERENT character, described below: do not copy the reference's armour, colours, face or pose, and do NOT copy how far its sword and shield are held out to the sides.

Geometry: heroic-scale tabletop miniature proportions: stout and chunky, slightly oversized head, hands, feet and held things; thick limbs; broad simple shapes; deep readable folds and plates rather than fine detail. Hands are simple chunky fists or mitten shapes. Every part thick enough to reconstruct as 3D geometry and to survive as a printed tabletop piece.
Held things: BROAD and chunky, never thin: wide blades, big heads on hammers, maces, staffs and spears, thick shafts. They are PALE or BRIGHT (bone-white wood, bright steel, cream, brass) against the clothes and skin, never plain dark wood-brown, so they show when the figure is seen small from above.
Finish: FULLY PAINTED in full colour, diffuse-first hand-painted game art with broad soft gradients, subtle brush texture, sparing painted edge highlights, low-frequency surface detail, mostly matte. A simple readable painted face.
Palette: rich but softened burgundy, moss green, ochre, cream, warm honey leather and wood, warm grey steel, used where they suit the figure. NO blue, teal or cyan anywhere on the figure (the background is a blue mask).
Avoid: grey unpainted primer, bare plastic or pewter, a bronze or stone statue look; photorealism, plastic toy gloss, strong reflections, black outlines, hard cel-shading bands, comic inking, flat vector art, anime or chibi proportions; thin fragile parts, loose straps, flying cloaks, long capes, banners, chains, feathers or hair strands sticking out; glow, magic effects, sparks, smoke; text, logos, emblems; multiple views, variants, a turnaround sheet or a grid in one image.

Pose: ONE single full figure, the WHOLE body in frame from the top of the head to the soles of the feet, standing still and upright in a clear, stable, compact classic miniature pose (not a T-pose, not an action leap, not a crouch, not a wide stance). Feet shoulder-width apart with a clear gap between the legs, planted FLAT on the same level. COMPACT: the whole figure, with everything it holds, fits inside an upright cylinder 8.5 ft across; NOTHING is held out to the side at arm's length. Whatever it holds is held UPRIGHT and close, a hand's width in front of or beside the body, with clear background visible in the gap, so nothing fuses together. Elbows near the ribs.
NO BASE: no base, no ground disc, no plinth, no pedestal, no rock, no grass tuft, no patch of floor under the feet. The figure floats on the plain background, standing on nothing. No cast shadow and no dark blob under the feet.

Presentation for image-to-3D: exactly one complete figure, centered, three-quarter FRONT view (turned about 30 degrees, face and chest clearly visible) from very slightly above eye level, generous clear space around every edge, perfectly uniform solid chroma-blue background, no horizon, no floor plane, no cast shadow, neutral even lighting with no colored light casts and no dark shadowed side, no environment, no scenery, no additional objects or other figures. The blue background is a removable mask and must not reflect blue light onto the figure.

Specific design: A frost giant, 20 ft tall: a towering, powerfully built giant with pale grey-WHITE skin (white, not blue), a huge white beard and hair in thick solid braids, a horned iron helmet with two thick short horns, a mantle of shaggy cream-white fur lying flat on the shoulders, a mail shirt and fur kilt, fur boots. BOTH hands hold a huge GREAT AXE upright in front of him, butt at ground level between his feet, one big bright crescent blade beside his head. Everything inside an 8.5-ft-wide cylinder.

gate.desc: one towering white-bearded giant in furs and a horned helmet holding one huge axe upright in front of him
must: the whole figure head to toe, both feet visible
a visible gap between the two legs
a horned helmet and a white beard
exactly one huge axe, complete end to end
fully painted in colour
must_not: any base, ground disc, plinth, pedestal, rock or patch of ground under the feet
a cast shadow or dark blob under the feet
the figure cropped by the frame anywhere (head, hat, weapon tip, feet, tail)
limbs fused together or fused to the body with no gap where the spec asks for a gap
a missing or broken held thing (something else carried as well is fine)
more than one figure, or several views of the figure
an unpainted grey, metal or stone statue look
a weapon or arm held far out to the side at arm's length
a rider, a second creature or scenery
